about: The record of the Job study3_freeze (transaction A, the content): every hash frozen before the scored run of study 3, the lead developer's decisions, the price table read again, the dataset fingerprint and image ids, and the free dry run of the full scored plan on the fake vendor client with legacy3.py on its bundle. Two dry runs were made: study3-freeze-dry-1 on 0d8b5ee, and study3-freeze-dry-2 on c5c4d96, after two code Jobs changed files the run executes (OpenAI cache writes, and OpenAI's long-context rates); the second binds the frozen code and the first is kept, superseded for code. The run folders, their request logs and the worker's scripts stay outside the repository in C:/esl/_study3/freeze/, cited by checksum. The frozen rows of the classification table and the frozen manifest follow in transaction B of the same Job, because a frozen path cannot enter a checkpoint. Task ids only: no question, key, schema text or transcript was read.

base.note: main when transaction A was prepared again. Since the first preparation on 5198bde two code Jobs landed: study3_openai_cache_write (93e0663) and study3_openai_long_context (c5c4d96). The mission worktree was removed and created again on c5c4d96, the dry run was run again on that commit, and the frozen bytes were written after it

decisions.openAICacheWrite: asked whether the OpenAI page's cache-write prices, where prices.json has 0.0, are a price change that stops the freeze: "Not a change, go on" (2026-11-21 UTC). Then, on the finding that the harness did not count OpenAI cache writes: "(a), code Job first" (2026-11-21 UTC), which became the Job study3_openai_cache_write
decisions.rerun: "Yes, re-run it" (W3, Coordinator session, 2026-11-21 UTC): the full scored plan's dry run again on the new code. The Job study3_openai_long_context (its follow-up W6) landed before the rerun, so one rerun covers both changes
decisions.removeWorktree: "Yes, discard and remove" (2026-11-22 UTC): worktree.py remove refused the old worktree with transaction A's uncommitted edits ("Checkout/index must be clean"); they were copied byte for byte to C:/esl/_study3/freeze/txA-draft-on-5198bde/ and discarded, and the worktree was created again on c5c4d96
decisions.rerunGoes: "Go" for Oracle, the Missions service and one build, then "Go" for study3-freeze-dry-2 (2026-11-22 UTC), each asked alone
decisions.freezeDate: "2026-11-22 (Recommended)" (2026-11-22 UTC): the frozen files carry the UTC date on which their bytes were written, after the second dry run; the price read keeps its own date, 2026-11-21
decisions.imageIds: the lead developer: "I believe every time we build an image the ids change, even though the content is identical. what matters is that we don't rebuild the images within the study"; study/launch/README.md records that every build writes new ids and that the rule is one build per study run (2026-11-21 UTC)
decisions.codeJobFirst: "Yes, code Job first" (2026-11-21 UTC): derive_a3.py had no freeze path; the Job study3_corpus3_frozen (5198bde) gave it --write --frozen before these edits
decisions.transactions: "Two in one mission" (2026-11-21 UTC): A the content, B the frozen rows, their golden pins and the frozen manifest
decisions.rationale: "Coordinator supplies it" (2026-11-21 UTC): the rationale of D068 to D074 from the study's private decision record

claude-sonnet-5-5.source: read from the Anthropic pricing page on 2026-10-20: input 2, five-minute cache write 2.50, cache hit 0.10 (0.05 times the input price for this model), output 10. No long-context rates: the Anthropic pricing page platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, Long context pricing (read 2026-11-21), says Claude 4.6 and later models except Claude Haiku 5.5 include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing

gpt-6.1-sol.source: OpenAI pricing page developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing read 2026-11-21, Standard tab, short context (up to 272K input tokens): input 2.00, cached input 0.10, 30m write 2.50, 12h write 5.00, output 10.00. The cache write is the 30-minute price: the prompt-caching guide developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching (read 2026-11-21) says the default lifetime is 30 minutes and the harness sets no lifetime; the Responses API reports the writes in usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens

long_context.source: read 2026-11-21: the model page developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol says API prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request; the pricing page developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, Standard tab, Long context (>272K input tokens): input 4.00, cached input 0.20, 30m write 5.00, 12h write 10.00, output 15.00. Neither page says whether 272K is 272,000 or 278,528 tokens; the threshold is 272,000 (decision L3), so a request between the two is priced long

prices.openAICacheWrites: cost includes OpenAI cache writes at 2.50 dollars per million tokens: the OpenAI client reads usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens into the cache-write class (the Job study3_openai_cache_write, 93e0663); the 30-minute price, the default lifetime, which the harness does not change
prices.longContext: each request is priced on its own: a gpt-6.1-sol request whose input (input + cached_read + cache_write) is above 272,000 tokens is priced at the long-context rates for the full request (input 4.00, cached read 0.20, cache write 5.00, output 15.00), every other request at the entry's own rates; claude-sonnet-5-5 has no long-context rates (the Job study3_openai_long_context, c5c4d96)

checkBeforeScoring.note: personnel200sBeforeFirstRun: the consecutive Personnel 200s before the first scored run of each of the 8 router-arm blocks (delta, epsilon), by the request log's timestamps against the run's start (finishedAt less elapsedSeconds): 13 in every block, which is every Personnel response before the first run. longestPersonnel200RunInSession: the longest such run over the whole session, later requests included.
